root_cause.text: The drm/gud atomic plane paths assumed `new_plane_state->fb` and `new_plane_state->crtc` were always non-NULL, so during USB disconnect `drm_atomic_helper_disable_all()` passed plane states with NULL framebuffer/CRTC and `gud_plane_atomic_check()`/`gud_plane_atomic_update()` dereferenced them, causing a kernel oops.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says disconnect calls `drm_atomic_helper_disable_all()` which “sets both the fb and crtc for a plane to NULL before invoking a commit,” and the patch removes unconditional use of `fb->format`, `drm_atomic_get_new_crtc_state(state, crtc)`, and `crtc->state`, replacing them with guards like `if (crtc) crtc_state = ...` and `if (!crtc || crtc->state->mode_changed || !crtc->state->enable)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix plane atomic checking to safely handle NULL CRTC/framebuffer states by avoiding unconditional dereferences and premature rejection.
intent_record.what: The function changes `crtc_state` from an uninitialized declaration to `struct drm_crtc_state *crtc_state = NULL;`, changes `format` from being immediately initialized with `fb->format` to a later-assigned declaration `const struct drm_format_info *format;`, removes the explicit warning/error checks that returned `-EINVAL` when `fb` or `crtc` were NULL, removes the unconditional call to `drm_atomic_get_new_crtc_state(state, crtc)`, removes the direct assignment `mode = &crtc_state->mode`, and replaces it with a conditional `if (crtc) crtc_state = drm_atomic_get_new_crtc_state(state, crtc);` before calling `drm_atomic_helper_check_plane_state()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer immediately rejects cases where the plane has no framebuffer or no CRTC, and it avoids dereferencing `crtc` when it is NULL by only fetching a CRTC state conditionally. This allows the atomic plane check path to handle disabled or detached plane states more safely and defer validation to the helper logic instead of forcing an early error.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize mode and format before the framebuffer format comparison so mode changes are detected using valid state.
intent_record.what: The assignments `mode = &crtc_state->mode;` and `format = fb->format;` were moved to immediately before the framebuffer format comparison, instead of occurring later after the rotation check.
intent_record.how: This ensures `format` and `mode` are initialized before they are used in the subsequent condition, preventing use of an uninitialized or stale `format` value when checking whether the framebuffer format changed and deciding whether to mark `crtc_state->mode_changed`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a NULL CRTC check in gud_plane_atomic_update() to avoid dereferencing crtc->state when no CRTC is attached.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding the update path in gud_plane_atomic_update() was expanded from checking only crtc->state->mode_changed and !crtc->state->enable to also first check whether crtc is NULL by adding !crtc to the if statement.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now safely handles cases where no CRTC is associated with the plane by taking the existing early handling path instead of dereferencing crtc->state, preventing a NULL pointer dereference and potential kernel crash.

grouping_result.intent: Fix plane atomic checking to safely handle NULL CRTC/framebuffer states by avoiding unconditional dereferences and premature rejection.
Initialize mode and format before the framebuffer format comparison so mode changes are detected using valid state.
Add a NULL CRTC check in gud_plane_atomic_update() to avoid dereferencing crtc->state when no CRTC is attached.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by making plane atomic check logic tolerate NULL framebuffer/CRTC states instead of unconditionally dereferencing or rejecting them, which is exactly what caused the disconnect-time kernel oops.

The change is about ordering initialization of mode/format for correct mode-change detection, not about handling NULL `fb`/`crtc` plane states during disconnect or preventing dereferences in the atomic plane check/update paths.

The root cause is missing NULL checks for plane_state->crtc/fb in GUD atomic plane paths during disconnect. This change directly adds a NULL CRTC guard in gud_plane_atomic_update(), preventing the exact kind of NULL dereference described.

candidates.rationale: This takes the CRTC from the new plane state in a path where the state may legitimately have no CRTC during disconnect; the subsequent logic assumes it is valid and leads to NULL-dereference conditions.
This fetches the framebuffer from the new plane state even when disconnect can produce a NULL fb, setting up the later unconditional dereference that triggers the crash.
This is the direct unconditional dereference of new_plane_state->fb via fb->format before validating fb, matching the root cause of assuming fb is always non-NULL.
This uses crtc without first handling the case where new_plane_state->crtc is NULL, contributing directly to the unsafe assumption in atomic check during disconnect.
This unconditionally dereferences crtc->state in atomic update, and crashes when the plane state has no attached CRTC during USB disconnect.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct NULL dereference in the atomic check path: during disconnect, new_plane_state->fb can be NULL, so accessing fb->format crashes exactly as described in the root cause.
This unconditionally dereferences crtc->state in the atomic update path. During disconnect, the plane state may have no attached CRTC, so this assumption causes the NULL dereference/oops.
This uses crtc derived from new_plane_state->crtc without first handling the valid disconnect case where it is NULL, contributing to the unsafe assumption in atomic check.
